author: Zach Fisher
title: Rep. Randy Feenstra says Congress is 'focused' on reducing insurance premiums - NewsBreak
text:
By Zach Fisher ,
1 hours ago
DES MOINES, Iowa (WHO) — In the last month of the year, the United States Congress is still working out tax credit extensions for the Affordable Care Act.
The tax credits were a part of the reason for the longest shutdown in federal government history. If calendars turn over to 2026 and some type of extension has not been passed, the average American can expect premium prices to go up.
“The majority of people, which is well over 65%, will see some changes in their premiums, about an average of $50 a month. So there is no change, that is a myth of a lie perpetuated by the Democrats in order to face something that they themselves did not think was important enough to do,” said Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R), IA-01. She made that comment three weeks ago , the day that Congress voted to reopen the government.
Since then, Congressman Zach Nunn (R), IA-03, signed on to cosponsor the Fix It Act , a bipartisan bill that would allow the tax credits to be extended for two years. If there is no tax credit extension, the no cap on income limits for applying will go back down to 400% above the federal poverty line.
Story continues below
Republicans have argued that some type of income cap is needed. Miller-Meeks believes that without an income cap, insurance companies have been raising premiums. Some Republicans liken that to the federal government subsidizing insurance companies, not give the companies any motivation to lower costs. Democrats argue that this standoff-like method will impact everyday Americans in the short term.
“Any time you’re dealing with tax credits, you have dollars going to corporations, going to health insurance companies, and they dramatically raise their costs or raise their premiums. And that’s exactly what has happened over the last decade. And that’s what we’ve got to stop. We want lower premiums, we want to make sure that people, come next year, they have lower premiums, and that is what I am focused on,” said Congressman Randy Feenstra (R), IA-04. Feenstra sits on the House Ways and Means committee, where the bill Nunn cosponsored is sitting.
Feenstra, when asked, did not say if he saw the Republicans’ plan as a slow play or a long play, adding that the Republicans have the majority and have to run the show.
He also discussed with WHO 13 News about his campaign for Iowa Governor, six months out from the primary elections. You can view Feenstra’s campaign talking points on his website . He expects his statewide tour to ramp up after the holiday season.
